diagnostics.notes: Both claims verified against their abstracts. Side A: short-term subgroup analysis of LCD vs normal/high-carbohydrate diet in type 2 diabetes, weight loss WMD -1.18 (95% CI -2.32, -0.04; P=0.04), described as effective. Side B: LCD vs HCD in adults with type 2 diabetes, weight explicitly reported as not differing significantly between groups. Same exposure class, same outcome domain, same between-group contrast; both are meta-analyses of RCTs. Side A's finding is a short-term subgroup result; side B reports the overall weight comparison without a significant difference. The authors' explicit no-difference conclusion in side B against a reported significant effect in side A takes the not_replicated branch.

source_evidence.quote: Subgroup analyses indicated that short term intervention of LCD was effective for weight loss (WMD: -1.18; 95% CI: -2.32, -0.04; P=0.04).
Changes in weight, HDL- and LDL-cholesterol, total cholesterol and blood pressure did not differ significantly between groups.

verdict.label: not_replicated
verdict.rationale: Both are meta-analyses of RCTs comparing low-carbohydrate diets with higher/normal-carbohydrate diets in type 2 diabetes for weight. Side A reports a significant short-term weight-loss effect (WMD -1.18; 95% CI -2.32, -0.04; P=0.04), while side B explicitly concludes that changes in weight did not differ significantly between LCD and HCD groups. An explicit no-difference conclusion against a reported effect yields not_replicated; the short-term subgroup framing in side A is a contextual note, not a text-supported explanation of the discrepancy.
